title: Rate limiting: why and where

kcs.statement: Rate limiting caps how many requests a client (identified by user, API key or IP) may make per time window, protecting backends from abuse, accidental overload and runaway cost.
A rate-limited HTTP request is rejected with status 429 Too Many Requests, ideally with a Retry-After header, and the limiter usually runs in the API gateway or middleware before business logic.
